title: Track
description: The movement of ONE THING over time: a person walking, a parcel in transit, a vehicle, a shared live position. Deliberately says nothing about WHY the thing moved — a run, a commute and a delivery are the same geometry, and the meaning belongs to whatever record points at the track. That separation is the whole purpose: two platforms had independently written byte-identical route blocks inside differently-named envelopes (a health Workout and a messenger's location share), so no reader arriving at a vault could tell that one shape served both. A record that owns the geometry and is its only owner may embed this shape inline instead of referencing a Track envelope; see `route`.

subject.description: The w3id of the THING that moved — a person, a parcel, a vehicle. Not necessarily an eName: a parcel's movement belongs to no account, and narrowing this to people is what forced the duplicate shapes in the first place.

agent.description: eName of whoever RECORDED the movement, when that is not the subject. A phone recording its owner, a carrier recording a parcel.

endedAt.description: When recording finished. Absent while it is still being appended to. NOTE that this is about the RECORDING and not about any permission: if the track exists because somebody shared their position for a window of time, that window lives on the record that points here, not on the track, so that one fact has one home.

route.description: The geometry itself. `format` names an entry in GeometryEncoding; `pointCount` is REQUIRED and is what separates 'empty' from 'could not decode', which is the only defence a reader has when it meets an encoding it does not implement.

format.description: An `id` from GeometryEncoding (504cacb9-79ef-498c-a352-e17830ed1876). Refuse one you do not know; never rewrite it.

data.description: The geometry, written in `format`. For geojson, the JSON text of a LineString; for polyline5, the encoded string.

pointCount.description: How many points the geometry holds. Required so that a reader which cannot decode `data` still knows whether there was anything to decode. Zero means genuinely empty.

samples.description: Per-point measurements, each array the SAME LENGTH as `pointCount` and in the same order. A samples array out of step with the geometry pairs one moment's speed with another place, silently, so a reader checks the lengths rather than trusting them. An absent array means not measured; a null entry means not measured at that point — never write zero or a default for an unknown, which would be indistinguishable from a real reading.

speed.description: Metres per second, as the device reported it.
